record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: If a cosmological spacetime has constant-mean-curvature initial data with positive Ricci 3-curvature, does the Einstein evolution preserve positivity of the Ricci curvature?

evidence.quote: Show that a cosmological spacetime with CMC initial data having positive Ricci 3-curvature, has an evolution which preserves Ricci positivity (S.T. Yau).

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $(M, g_0, K_0)$ be initial data for the vacuum Einstein equations on a closed 3-manifold $M$, where $g_0$ is a Riemannian metric and $K_0$ is a symmetric 2-tensor (the second fundamental form) satisfying the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints. Assume the data are of constant-mean-curvature (CMC) type, i.e. $\mathrm{tr}_{g_0} K_0$ is constant on $M$, and assume that the spacetime $(\bar M, \bar g)$ obtained by maximal globally hyperbolic vacuum Einstein evolution of $(M, g_0, K_0)$ is cosmological (globally hyperbolic with compact Cauchy surfaces and satisfying the strong energy condition). Suppose further that the Ricci curvature of $g_0$ is positive definite. Question: along the CMC foliation (or any Cauchy development) of the resulting spacetime, is positivity of the Ricci curvature of the induced spatial metric $g_t$ preserved for all times $t$ within the maximal development?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not turn up a resolution of this problem (attributed to S.-T. Yau) concerning preservation of positive 3-Ricci curvature under cosmological CMC Einstein evolution. Related work addresses existence and non-existence of CMC Cauchy surfaces and spacetime splitting, but no explicit proof or counterexample to this Ricci-positivity preservation question was found, so the status appears unresolved based on available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Existence of CMC Cauchy surfaces and spacetime splitting
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses existence of CMC Cauchy surfaces in cosmological spacetimes and splitting theorems, but does not address preservation of Ricci positivity under evolution.
status_evidence.claim: Related literature on CMC surfaces in cosmological spacetimes does not establish the preservation of positive Ricci 3-curvature.

status_evidence.title: Examples of cosmological spacetimes without CMC foliations
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs cosmological spacetimes lacking CMC Cauchy hypersurfaces, but no statement about preservation of positive Ricci curvature.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the Ricci-positivity preservation question is given.
